name: The National
label: 4AD
lede: Five Ohioans in Brooklyn pooled $15,000 for a debut, kept their day jobs through two records, then quit them. Two decades on they win Grammys, and their guitarist worked on most of Taylor Swift's Folklore.

hero.by: The National at Primavera Sound, 2022. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Two sets of brothers and a tall friend
eras.text: Matt Berninger and Scott Devendorf met studying graphic design in Cincinnati; the Dessner twins and Bryan Devendorf had played in bands together since they were kids. They all ended up in Brooklyn, kept their jobs, and started a label to put out their own record.

years.h: A Cincinnati garage band named after Berninger's mother
years.p: Berninger and Scott Devendorf meet in the University of Cincinnati design program and start Nancy, which wants to sound like [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]]. It lasts five years and one album, Ruther 3429.

years.h: Project Nim ends, and the Dessners and Devendorfs regroup in Brooklyn
years.p: After [[Aaron Dessner|1890e726-4817-42f4-92e7-ca78bef6692a]] and Bryan Devendorf's band Project Nim broke up in 1998, they joined Berninger and Scott Devendorf in New York.
years.xp:
Several of them kept day jobs, some in the dot-com boom. They played free Sunday-night shows at Luna Lounge on the Lower East Side.

The website is americanmary.com because of a song on the first record. Berninger once said they never thought of changing it, "although we should have."

years.src: Brassland: The National · Wikipedia: The National
years.h: A $15,000 debut on their own label
years.p: The band pooled the money and released it on Brassland, the label the Dessner twins started with Alec Hanley Bemis. [[Bryce Dessner|20336142-85de-4e11-a1fd-a6c815b4e583]] helped record it and soon joined for good.
years.xp: Brassland's own page describes the band as "two sets of brothers and one tall, blonde best friend." No Depression called the songs "Americana bar-soaked gems."

years.h: Dust from the towers settles on the unsold boxes
years.p: The CDs had been shipped to a Brooklyn apartment that summer. After September 11, Brassland recalls, dust from the wreckage coated the boxes.

years.h: Mercury Lounge, then the first tour of America
years.p: The National play the Lower East Side room and head out on their first US tour.

eras.title: Quitting the day jobs
eras.text: Sad Songs for Dirty Lovers began the long partnership with producer Peter Katis and found fans in France before America. In 2004 the five quit their jobs and signed to Beggars Banquet, and Alligator did the rest, slowly.

years.h: Sad Songs for Dirty Lovers breaks in France first
years.p: The first record with Katis and Paul Heck came out in France on Talitres, and DJ Bernard Lenoir had them on his France Inter Black Sessions. Uncut and the Chicago Tribune named it album of the year.

years.src: Wikipedia: The National · Clash: Alligator turns 20
years.h: Cherry Tree EP, and a tour with the Walkmen
years.p: The EP previews "All the Wine." The band then quit their day jobs and signed to Beggars Banquet, because running their own label had become "too complicated."
years.xp:
Aaron Dessner looked back on the Brassland years in Clash: they made the records themselves, started a label, booked the shows "and fell on our face."

Berninger had been doing well in advertising. He gave it up in his thirties for the band.

years.src: Clash: Alligator turns 20 · Wikipedia: The National
years.h: Alligator, made in Aaron Dessner's house
years.p: Much of the Beggars Banquet debut was recorded at Dessner's place on Stratford Road in Ditmas Park, where Berninger rented the upstairs duplex. Vincent Moon shot the blurry close-up of Berninger on the cover.
years.xp: It took a while. Dessner told Clash it was a year before it "started to seep into people's consciousness." Then came sold-out nights at the Troubadour and Webster Hall, and Pitchfork and NME later put it among the best albums of the 2000s.

years.big: "We're not the B-side to Interpol any more."
q: Whelan's turned our heads a little bit.
years.h: An encore at Whelan's in Dublin
years.p: Berninger, to Guardian readers, on the 2005 Dublin show where the crowd called them back. Until then, he said, they'd ridden the fumes of the New York scene.

eras.title: Boxer goes to the campaign trail
eras.text: Boxer was the record critics put on their decade lists. One of its songs scored an Obama campaign video, the band opened for R.E.M., and when Beggars Banquet folded into 4AD, the National went with it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Boxer · Guardian: Matt Berninger reader interview
years.h: [[Sufjan Stevens|01d3c51b-9b98-418a-8d8e-37f6fab59d8c]] drops by to play piano on Boxer
years.p: Recorded mostly at Katis's Tarquin Studios in Bridgeport, Connecticut, with home sessions in Brooklyn and West Virginia. It debuted at No. 68 with about 9,500 copies, and Paste made it the album of the year.
years.xp:
Stevens plays on "Racing Like a Pro" and "Ada"; Berninger called it a one-day thing that happened because they lived in the same neighbourhood. It's also the first album where his wife, Carin Besser, writes lyrics with him.

Berninger said Katis "jumps in as a seventh member." The Guardian later put Boxer at No. 68 on its 100 best albums of the 21st century.

years.h: Why a band called the National got boycotted in Germany
years.p: Berninger explained in 2007 that they chose a name that meant nothing. In Germany some shows were boycotted by people who took it for a far-right connection, and the band had to do press to say otherwise.

years.h: Boxer takes the band to Latitude
years.p: The Boxer tour runs through the UK festival circuit in 2007. A year later it's Coachella, Glastonbury, Roskilde and Lollapalooza.

years.h: "Fake Empire" scores an Obama campaign video
years.p: An instrumental version runs under "Signs of Hope and Change," and the song plays at the Democratic convention. The band sells "Mr. November" shirts and gives the proceeds to the campaign.
years.xp: They played a rally on Cincinnati's Fountain Square with [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]] on October 16, 2008, with buses taking people to vote early. In 2010 they played to more than 25,000 before an Obama speech in Madison, Wisconsin.

years.cap: Berninger at the Hammerstein Ballroom, New York, October 2008
years.h: Opening for R.E.M., with Modest Mouse
years.p: The National support [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]] on the Accelerate tour. In May, Vincent Moon's film A Skin, a Night comes out on DVD with The Virginia EP.

years.cap: The National at the Brooklyn Academy of Music
years.h: The Dessners' Dark Was the Night raises over $1 million
years.p: The twins produce the 31-track Red Hot AIDS benefit for 4AD, now the band's label after Beggars Banquet merged into it. Arcade Fire, Feist, Sufjan Stevens and David Byrne are on it.

eras.title: No. 3 on Billboard, and a brother with a camera
eras.text: High Violet, made in Aaron Dessner's garage, opened at No. 3 in America. The band got bigger rooms, a Grammy nomination, a six-hour art piece at MoMA PS1, and a documentary by the singer's younger brother.

years.src: Wikipedia: High Violet · Wikipedia: The National
years.h: High Violet opens at No. 3
years.p: Recorded from March 2009 to January 2010, much of it in Aaron Dessner's garage in Ditmas Park, and released on 4AD. It sold 51,000 copies in the first week and won the Q award for best album.

years.h: Coachella, then a song for Gerard Smith
years.p: On April 20 in Kansas City, the band dedicated "About Today" to [[TV on the Radio|eb872766-98f6-453d-883f-2ae908a18315]]'s [[Gerard Smith|7cd3810b-7312-4294-b40d-69a6511b042d]], who had died of lung cancer that day.

years.h: The National record "The Rains of Castamere" for Game of Thrones
years.p: It plays over the end of the season-two episode "Blackwater." The same year brings covers for Boardwalk Empire and Bob's Burgers.

years.cap: The National at Alexandra Palace, London, November 2013
years.src: Wikipedia: Mistaken for Strangers · Wikipedia: The National
years.h: Tom Berninger's roadie film premieres at Tribeca
years.p: Matt hired his younger brother for the 2010 crew; Tom filmed the tour, and himself trying to make a film. Pitchfork called Mistaken for Strangers the funniest, most meta music movie since Spinal Tap.
years.xp: Carin Besser edited it. The Washington Post called it a poignant picture of art, family, self-sabotage and the "prickly intricacies of brotherly love." It went to theatres in March 2014.

yt: Ragnar Kjartansson and the National at PS1
years.h: "Sorrow," 105 times in six hours at MoMA PS1
years.p: Icelandic artist Ragnar Kjartansson had the band play the High Violet song over and over for a whole afternoon. It came out as a vinyl box set in 2015.

years.h: Trouble Will Find Me is the one they "really enjoyed making"
years.p: Aaron Dessner's phrase for it. The album opened at No. 3 in the US, Canada and the UK and was nominated for the Grammy for best alternative album.

years.h: Saturday Night Live, at last
years.p: Their first SNL, with host Lena Dunham: "Graceless" and "I Need My Girl."

years.cap: Aaron Dessner at Edmonton Folk Fest
years.h: Aaron Dessner and Justin Vernon start a festival in Wisconsin
years.p: Eaux Claires, curated with [[Bon Iver|437a0e49-c6ae-42f6-a6c1-84f25ed366bc]]'s [[Justin Vernon|0f1d5b01-8784-4870-9bd6-fa43178b9441]], has the National as a headliner. Dessner and Vernon also make records together as Big Red Machine.

eras.title: A barn upstate and a Grammy
eras.text: Aaron Dessner bought an 18th-century barn in the Hudson Valley and turned it into Long Pond studio. Sleep Well Beast was made there and won a Grammy; in 2020 Taylor Swift's Folklore was too, mostly by email.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sleep Well Beast · Wikipedia: The National
years.h: Sleep Well Beast goes to No. 2
years.p: Recorded at Long Pond and in Paris, Los Angeles and Berlin. Berninger said he and Besser wrote much of it about the hard parts of their own marriage.
years.xp: "The System Only Dreams in Total Darkness" became the band's first No. 1 on a Billboard songs chart, Adult Alternative Songs, in August 2017. Pentagram designed a corporate-style identity for the album around a pentagon drawn from the barn.
play: The System Only Dreams in Total Darkness

years.src: Wikipedia: The National · Wikipedia: Sleep Well Beast
years.h: Scott Devendorf accepts the Grammy for the band
years.p: Sleep Well Beast wins best alternative music album. The same year the band writes the songs for Erica Schmidt's stage musical Cyrano, starring Peter Dinklage.

years.src: Wikipedia: The National · Guardian: Matt Berninger reader interview
years.h: I Am Easy to Find arrives with a Mike Mills film
years.p: Mills directed a short of the same name starring Alicia Vikander, scored with different arrangements of the album's songs. Berninger later called it a long record.

years.cap: Aaron Dessner at All Points East, London
years.h: Taylor Swift asks Aaron Dessner to write with her
years.p: Swift contacted him in late April 2020. He worked on 11 of the 16 songs on Folklore from the Hudson Valley while she sang in Los Angeles, and it won the Grammy for album of the year.
years.xp:
They had met at SNL in 2014, and Swift talked to the twins at a National show in 2019 about how the band writes: Dessner makes the music and sends it to the singer. She said they were in touch daily for three or four months.

The band itself appears on "Coney Island" on Evermore, the follow-up, which both Dessners co-produced.

q: I was attracted to the music that was the most self-soothing.
years.src: Guardian: Matt Berninger reader interview · Wikipedia: First Two Pages
years.h: Berninger stops being able to write
years.p: Berninger told Guardian readers he hadn't felt that sad since he was a kid. For a long stretch, he couldn't come up with lyrics or melodies at all.
years.xp:
He said he's always lived with a normal level of anxiety and depression, but 2021 was different: he didn't want to leave the house. He described it as an illness, and said the closing song of the next album, "Send for Me," was written for people who were there for him.

The Wikipedia article on First Two Pages of Frankenstein quotes him saying it was the first time he feared the band had come to an end.

eras.title: Two albums in one year
eras.text: The National came back to the stage with songs still unfinished and worked them out live. Two albums followed in 2023, one of them announced three days before it came out.

years.cap: Berninger at All Points East, London, August 2022
years.h: First show in two and a half years, in Pamplona
years.p: At Baluarte the band plays three new songs, including the one that became "Weird Goodbyes." That single, with Bon Iver, comes out in August.

years.src: Wikipedia: First Two Pages · Guardian: Matt Berninger reader interview
years.h: Taylor Swift co-writes "The Alcott" with Berninger
years.p: Made mostly at Long Pond, with Swift, [[Phoebe Bridgers|96855c21-b832-4366-ba12-0d2330c36a86]] and Sufjan Stevens as guests. Berninger said they wanted it short and punchy.

years.cap: The National at Primavera Sound, Barcelona
years.h: Berninger on climbing into crowds: the garbage can incident
years.p: He told Guardian readers he has climbed bars, balconies and hotel windows mid-song, and once sang the rest of a song inside a garbage can after the lid gave way.

years.h: Laugh Track is announced on a Friday and out on Monday
years.p: The surprise album was revealed at the band's Homecoming festival in Cincinnati on September 15. It ends with "Smoke Detector," which grew out of a soundcheck.

years.cap: Berninger and Dessner at a campaign rally, Madison, Wisconsin, October 2024
years.h: Rome, a live double album
years.p: Recorded at the Auditorium Parco della Musica. The band says the next studio album will be loose and improvised, built from soundcheck jams Berninger has been pushing.

years.h: Berninger's second solo record, Get Sunk
years.p: It follows Serpentine Prison (2020) and his EL VY album with Brent Knopf.
